full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Hamidul Haque, J: By this rule opposite parties were called upon to show cause as to why the detenu Lipi Begum Wife of Mansur Ali now detained in Tangail District Jail in judicial custody in connection with Mirzapur P.S. Case No. 3(8)2000 should not be brought before this court to satisfy itself that the same detenue is being held in custody without lawful authority. 

 2. In this rule the petitioner is the husband of Lipi Begum, victim of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 305/2000 of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat Tangail. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the victim was most illegally given to the custody of the lather though the petitioner is legal husband of the victim Lipi Begum. He has further submitted that the victim is already 17 years old and as such she is legally able to take decision regarding her own custody. 

 3. The informant-opposite party appeared by filing an affidavit-in-opposition and the learned Advocate has submitted that the present petitioner is 11w main accused in the above case and he is an absconder and as such a fugitive and no relief can be given on the basis of the application filed by a fugitive. 

 5. We have perused the order dated 9.10.2000 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Tangail in Criminal Misc Case No. 801/2000. In the present application under Section-491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the petitioner prays for giving a direction to the jail authority, Tangail to set the detenu Lipi Beguin at liberty. She was at first given to the custody of her it her l)y the above order but when the victim did not go to the custody of her father, she was put into judicial custody. So, a question arose that when the detenu was detained in judicial custody by order of a court, whether her detention can be considered as illegal unless and until the order of that court is set aside by a higher court. 

 6. Mr. Kazi Shahadat Hossain has argued that the detention can be declared illegal in this proceeding under Section-491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in this regard he referred to the case of Jhosna Rani Saha Vs. Khandaker Jayedill as reported in 52 D.L.R (AD) page 6C and also the case of Dr. Kazi Mozammel Haque Vs. The State as reported in 45 DLR page 197. We have carefully gone through both the reported eases and we have rot ta6 that the above question was not agitated in any of these two cases. So, we are of the view that the decision given in those cases have no manner of application regarding the above question. The High Court Division in exercise of the power given under Section-491(1)(b) of the Code may set at liberty a person who is found to detained illegally or improperly. But when a person is put into custody by an order of a court it cannot be said that his custody is illegal or improper unless or until that order is set aside by a Superior Court. 

 8. Mr. K.S. Hossain has pointed out that no appeal lies against the order of the learned Sessions Judge and as such the proper forum is to come under Section-491. We cannot also accept this view because if no appeal lies in that case there is provision of revision and this court in its revisional jurisdiction cant set aside the order of the Subordinate Court. 

 9. To our knowledge, we could not find any authority or decision of this court on this particular point. However, we have considered the decision given in a case by the Madras High Court reported in 33 Cr1. L.J. page 49. In this case we find that the mother of an illegimate child filed an application under Section-491 of the Code for handing over the custody of the child to her. The mother was not found legal guardian of the child by a competent court and on this ground the court held that in the face of the subsisting order passed by a competent court, the mother of the child the petitioner has no remedy by way of habeas corpus unless it was shown that the detention of the minor child by appointed guardian was illegal. The court further observed as follows 

 10. The other ease which we have considered is the case reported in 1982 p page 1029 (Karachi). In this case custody of the detenu was handed over to the respondent by an order passed by an Additional City Magistrate. The court held that as the custody of the detenu was handed over to the respondent by a competent court, the petitioner under Section-491 of the Code was not maintainable unless the order passed by the Additional City Magistrate was set. aside by a competent Appellate Court So, we find from the above decisions and also from the plain reading of the provisions of Section-491(1)(b) of the Code that when the order of custody of the detenu is passed by a competent court, a petitioner cannot get any relief under Section-491 of the Code unless and until that order is set aside by a superior court.
